instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks. Slice the carrot into thin rounds. Dice the onion, slice the garlic, and chop the dill fronds.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft but not brown.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens a shade.
Add the potatoes, carrot, peas, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, the rest of the olive oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Stir well.
Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to medium-low. Cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Take the lid off and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are tender when you pierce them and most of the liquid is gone. The sauce should be thick and glossy with oil.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the dill.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve warm or at room temperature, in bowls.
method_notes: The lead (Not Quite Nigella) and the other two versions all braise peas, potatoes and carrot in olive oil and tomato, finish with dill and cook until the liquid is nearly gone. They differ on tomato (paste and canned, fresh grated, or puree), on stock versus water, and on a side of feta and bread. I used vegetable broth as the lead does (it calls for chicken or vegetable), kept the lead's tomato paste step, and left off the feta and bread so the dish stays vegan and gluten-free. Not Quite Nigella's rating (5 from 54) is the page's visible rating; Olive Tomato and Dimitra's Dishes show no star rating.
